candidates.title: Performance
candidates.text:
Cities: Skylines II is built for the future with modern hardware in mind, allowing us to add more depth and detail to the game than its predecessor had. Earlier this month, we shared a note on performance as we had not reached the benchmark target we had set for the game. Following this, we have seen some concerns about performance and what it means for the game as a whole. We’d like to give some context to the issues the game is currently facing, what we’re doing to address them, and what you can do if you are among the players experiencing performance issues.

Firstly, we want to assure you that the issues are not deeply rooted in the game’s foundation, so we fully expect to be able to improve performance going forward. The issues we are currently facing are tied to the rendering of the game, and decreasing the quality of visual effects such as Depth of Field, Global Illumination, and Volumetrics will get you a fair performance without affecting simulation - at the cost of some eye candy. If you experience low FPS we recommend the following:

- Reduce screen resolution to 1080p
- Disable Depth of Field and Volumetrics
- Reduce Global Illumination
- Check the full guide for more tips

WHAT HAPPENS POST-RELEASE

Following the release, we intend to push a series of small patches (and likely a big one) as we significantly improve different areas of performance. candidates.title: Dev Diary 187 - Performance & Optimization
candidates.text:
Now let’s get back to the regular schedule and start digging into the details

First, we need to define what we mean when we say speed or performance. Normally, when we talk about performance, we refer to two categories: rendering and simulation. When developing DLCs for Grand Strategy Games, we create more systems and objects to simulate over time. Graphical complexity will also increase with more development, but during DLC development it rarely causes new bottlenecks for us.

However, increased simulation demands put more load on the CPU for calculations and data transformations due to new features and systems to keep track of. This makes the CPU our most common bottleneck when it comes to optimizing for simulation tick speed. So our most common task when it comes to optimizing the code for our games is to look at where our CPU-cycles are spent and where we can be more efficient, in order to keep down the average time-per-tick for a playthrough.

This makes the time-per-tick measurement the most important metric for us to track throughout development, and the one we will be talking about the most in this Dev Diary.

Measuring Performance

So how do you get accurate measurements for tick speed when working with a complex simulation? There are many variables in play that will affect the final outcome. Examples of variables that affect results include: graphical settings, hardware, test length, early- or late-game state, background tasks, and random variation.

All of these variables matter in analyzing how the game performs, but we also want to stress that most of our performance improvements are going to have a similar effect across the board of different hardware. For that reason, the most valuable test is early-game tick performance on fixed hardware with fixed settings and a fixed random seed. This gives us a test that we can quickly repeat to allow us to track the tick speed trends over time for different versions of the code during development and allows us to quickly spot degradations.

candidates.title: Tuning Your PC For Tactics
candidates.text:
These settings affect how the game is run and can have a significant impact on performance. To make sure a wide range of PC specifications were supported, The Coalition worked with Intel on specific optimizations. Two areas that offer broad performance improvements are covered here.

Variable Rate Shading
Variable Rate Shading (or VRS), is a relatively new technique. It’s used to adjust the number of pixels affected by a pixel shader, which is a fragment of code that runs on every pixel drawn to the screen.
With VRS, surrounding pixels can also be affected by a pixel shader, resulting in less overall work for the GPU. Working with Intel, this setting was built to improve performance without making a highly noticeable change to image quality.

Async Compute
Async Compute is a method of running graphics workloads in parallel. Working with Intel, this setting has been expanded from a similar implementation in Gears 5 to support more workloads in parallel across different types of hardware.

BENCHMARK

All these settings come together to make Gears Tactics a game that will run well across low power hardware and scale up for the highest end gaming rigs.

Use the built-in benchmark to preview the games visuals and performance with custom settings, or check how the game will perform at recommended settings for your hardware.

Here’s a sample of the performance you’ll be able to experience across a range of devices using the games recommended settings.

This thin and light laptop uses Variable Rate Shading in order to achieve over 30 FPS at 900p.

candidates.title: Vol.69 - Ready or Not Development Briefing
candidates.text:
Once again, there are many factors that will be considered in these sorts of AI-related experimental discussions going forward. You can expect a comprehensive analysis of our approaches as we carefully vet and solidify specific development routes.

Optimization:

Optimization remains a high priority to ensure the game is running as smoothly as possible for as many systems as possible.

Although we've made much progress already, we are currently working on improved scalability settings, LOD ‘impostors’, shader caching, and other performance factors. We’d also like to give a bit of context regarding unlisted backend performance changes recently included in Hotfix #4.

This is to give you all an idea of some of the work that’s being done for the future, however they may be implemented at different times and are still subject to change.

Scalability settings:

Scalability settings are the graphics options that let you optimize performance on your system, for example turning on/off specific graphics features or setting them to high/low. We are revisiting these scaling settings because currently they do not adequately differentiate between High/Medium/Low qualities in terms of both visuals and FPS.

The goal is to provide players with more tailored options that better suit their hardware capabilities, allowing more visual trade-off for higher performance at very low settings.

For example, we plan to make the “streaming pool” value, which affects texture quality depending on how high or low the value is, to be more dynamic based on graphics settings.

LOD “impostors:”

The word “impostors” is not a typo, but instead a way to refer to the 2D Level of Detail (LOD) elements that are included on distant foliage, rocks, or other pieces of environmental art. These 2D elements are carefully used at a distance to improve performance while mimicking the detail of 3D models without looking too sus.

candidates.title: Addressing concerns related to optimization of Last Train Home
candidates.text:
Hi, Legionaries,

We would like to formally address the issues related to optimization that were reported to us via different channels during the Steam Next Fest.

First and foremost, thank you for playing the demo of Last Train Home and getting back to us with your feedback. It’s very valuable to us in enhancing the game's performance and user experience.

The issues some of you faced include:

- Crashes, freezes, severe FPS drops, and prolonged loading times when trying to start a new journey. - It seems these issues happen for specific architectures and combinations of graphic settings. We are thankful for every report via Redmine as they help us track these issues and come up with solutions. But we'd also like to point out that during the Steam Next Fest, only 0.5 percent of the player base encountered crashes.
- FPS drops, freezes, and even crashes during gameplay – It seems this happens more often when using more monitors, especially when they have substantially different types of graphics cards and are handled by different built-in tools. Also, when putting the game in the background often and using certain combinations of graphics settings.
- Memory leaks when playing for many hours with lots of save/load.

What can you do?

- Before downloading the demo, make sure to check the minimal hardware requirements for playing the game on our Steam page.
- Make sure all your drivers are up to date (AMD, Nvidia, Windows Updates...).
- If you encounter any issues, bugs, or crashes, while playing the demo, we kindly request that you report them via Redmine by following the provided instructions at this link.
- If you experience a crash, you should also receive a prompt asking you if the information about the crash can be forwarded to us. Please do so. This information will be critical for us to address the issue.

To come to the point, we are aware of the problems and are diligently working to address them before the game's official release planned for November 28. We will update even the Demo build itself.

candidates.title: City Corner #4 - A Peek into Performance
candidates.text:
Issues in the game can also cause bigger performance problems. Some of these we have already fixed, like the citizens or criminals getting stuck in certain buildings, which caused excessive pathfinding, or the large amount of bicycles, which also caused further stress on the pathfinding system. However, there are still similar problems to be found to improve the performance further.

[img src=" align="center"]Unity Profiler is used to track the Pathfinding performance bottlenecks. In this case, many of the CPU threads are busy with pathfinding and related calculations.

Steps towards better performance

In our previous updates, we have applied some simple fixes related to performance. For example, lowering shadow resolution on lower hardware settings, automatically matching the graphics quality setting based on the used hardware, and disabling some of the most taxing effects, like SSGI, on lower-end hardware.

While the performance issues still need more investigation, optimization, and trying out different solutions, we do have a rough idea of what we should prioritize when it comes to improving the performance. We are currently prioritizing the LODs and the algorithms that affect the rendering, which will improve the performance on the GPU side and can immediately be seen even in your smallest cities. We are also looking into the limitations of different CPUs and graphics cards.

We have prepared a benchmark tool, which allows you to check your performance between patches and how the updates affect the performance on your computer. This also allows us to gather data on which areas and on what kind of hardware we need to put more focus on. This will be included in the next patch, which, if all goes well, is planned to be released at the end of this month.

[img src=" align="center"]An early iteration of the benchmark tool.

Thank you for reading, and as always, we will keep you updated on the progress as we make changes towards better performance. Until next time!

Hey everyone,

Today we are adding support for NVIDIA DLSS 3 to Marvel's Spider-Man Remastered. This technology for GeForce RTX 40 Series GPUs combines DLSS Super Resolution, DLSS Frame Generation and NVIDIA Reflex to boost your frame rate. We also plan to make latency reducing technology NVIDIA Reflex available to other RTX GPU users with a future patch.

Hardware-accelerated GPU scheduling must be activated in Windows to use DLSS Frame Generation. In Windows 11, this option is turned on by default. To enable this feature in Windows 10, press the Windows key on your keyboard, type Graphics settings and press enter. This opens the Graphics settings menu. Here you can enable Hardware-accelerated GPU scheduling. A restart is required to activate the feature.

This update also addresses an issue that would make cutscenes in the game slow down when no audio device was detected, or when an audio device was removed. The patch also contains a fix for a crash that could occur on some hardware configurations when using Very High ray-tracing settings.

candidates.title: Finishing Move/Call of Duty: Black Ops 6
candidates.text: During the Open Beta, preview videos were available for the two default Finishing Moves. Following the release of Season One, each Finishing Move can be previewed in each Operator's customization menu in real-time. Most of the Finishing Move preview icons feature Marshall as the attacker and Stone as the victim. In the actual previews, the game uses either the player's currently equipped Operator, or the featured Operator if previewed via a bundle containing an Operator skin, as the attacker. In bundles without an Operator skin, a Finishing Move preview will use Nazir or Caine as the attacker. In the Open Beta preview videos, Adler was seen as the attacker for the Finishing Moves. Finishing Moves from crossover characters usually feature said characters as the attackers on the icon (e.g. the "T-800 Style" Finishing Move features the T-800). Interestingly, the "Roped Up" Finishing Move, which features the Front Man, featured a different icon with Marshall as the attacker on Warzone Mobile prior to the Season Two update. All Finishing Move previews in the Battle Passes and seasonal Events feature a different Operator as the attacker instead of Marshall: Sev in Season One, Nocturne in Season Two, John Black Ops in Season Three, Stitch in Season Four, Sims in Season Five, and the Predator in Season Six. In Warzone, when equipping a Modern Warfare II or Modern Warfare III Operator and previewing a Black Ops 6 Finishing Move via a bundle, it is possible for the equipped Operator to appear as the attacker, even though it is not possible to have such a combination in-game. Prior to the Season Two update, the "Gentleman's Handshake" Finishing Move erroneously used the same preview icon as the "Batter Up" Finishing Move.

The Universal Carrier was one of the most common British armoured vehicles of WWII, with around 113,000 units built. It was developed from earlier Bren Gun and Scout Carriers, but the Universal design introduced in 1940 gave the British Army a single flexible tracked vehicle suited for many roles. It was small, open-topped, lightly armoured, and powered by a Ford V8 engine. Its usual crew included three or four men, with space for weapons, ammunition, stores, or passengers. The carrier was not meant to be a tank. Its value came from mobility and practicality. British and Commonwealth units used it to move Bren guns, Boys anti-tank rifles, PIATs, mortars, radios, and observation teams. In infantry battalions, carrier platoons gave commanders a fast way to shift support weapons across the battlefield. Reconnaissance units also used carriers beside scout cars. The vehicle appeared in nearly every theatre, from the Western Desert to Burma and Northwest Europe. Many variants were built, including mortar carriers, artillery observation vehicles, and the Wasp flamethrower version. Its simple design made it easy to adapt, which explains why it served long after WWII.

In KARDS, Universal Carrier brings that same versatility to the battlefield. It reduces the cost of your Plans and rewards every Plan played with a Blast. Simple, reliable, and always ready for the next task.

candidates.title: Oceania Storm: Britain and Germany
candidates.text:
Area bombardment became a central part of RAF Bomber Command’s night war against Germany. Early hopes of striking individual factories or military targets often failed due to darkness and poor weather. The 1941 Butt Report used photographs to measure results and showed how often crews missed their aiming points. Many bombs fell far from the intended target, which pushed the RAF toward attacks on wider industrial areas rather than single buildings. This did not mean the RAF gave up trying to improve accuracy. In 1942 it created the Pathfinder Force, made up of selected crews who flew ahead of the main bomber group. Their job was to locate the target and mark it with flares and target indicators. They also received navigation systems such as Gee, Oboe, and H2S earlier than many other units. In 1943, the force was redesignated No. 8 Group, with the motto “We Guide to Strike”. The Pathfinders helped concentrate area bombardment and reduced the waste caused by scattered bombing.

In KARDS, Area Bombardment delivers a Lancaster Mk I directly to your support line before shuffling it back into your deck at the end of the turn. One heavy bomber exactly when you need it, with the possibility of another sortie later. Flexible, efficient, and capable of delivering overwhelming force at the decisive moment.

Germany

Germany had little direct role in the Pacific Theater, focusing on naval engagements and occasional raiding, but its forces fought across some of the harshest battlefields of the war, from the deserts of North Africa and the mountains of Italy to the vast, unforgiving expanses of the Eastern Front.

In Oceania Storm, Germany focuses on operating units repeatedly and extracting maximum value from Veteran units. The longer your forces remain active, the greater the pressure they can exert.

Designations for mining are under the "D" menu, building is under "B", then "W" for workshops. When mining you can press "X" to cancel designations in a specific area. candidates.title: Dune: Spice Wars FAQ
candidates.text:
We’ve announced House Harkonnen and House Atreides as playable factions. We’re planning to have 2 other factions at launch, followed by a 5th faction during Early Access (and more later!).

Why is the House Atreides green in game when in previous games it was blue?

To stay true to the books. Many things in Dune have been represented differently in shows, movies, comics or games over the years. The Atreides banner and uniforms are described as green and black in the books so that’s what we went for in the game.

Will houses from classic Dune games make their way to the game? (House Ordos...)

House Ordos was first mentioned in the Dune Encyclopedia and then in the video game Dune 2, but never in Frank Herbert’s works. We’re starting with what’s in the books, and we’ll see what would be best beyond that during the Early Access.

What similarities does the game have with your other title, Northgard?

Both games are real time games with a slower pace. Beyond that the games are quite different. Dune Spice Wars is on a much bigger scale, featuring politics, trading, covert operations and a deeper resource management system. Game length is also 2 to 3 times longer than Northgard (although this could still change at this point).

Have you taken any inspiration from previous Dune games for this title?

We’ve played all the Dune video games (Dune and Dune 2 especially) and all board games as well so there will be some influence. That said, Dune Spice Wars is very much its own game with a unique take on the struggle for the control of Arrakis.

candidates.title: Dune: Spice Wars review
candidates.text: As I am slowly getting familiar with Dune: Spice Wars I feel it is surprisingly refreshing. A RTS game with so many unorthodox features that it feels both familiar and foreign at the same time.It borrows from classic RTS games, boardgames, card games and then adds some of its own to create a unique experience.You can choose between a full campaign or a shorter match. The full campign is essentially your chance to play out the battle for Arrakis as one of 5 major sides of the conflict. If you are familiar with the Dune universe you will recognize the factions, leaders and advisors you can select. In my opinion they fit very well with their descriptions in the books and offer a great variety of playstyles. Very far from Dune 2, where your options were essentially just 3 paint colors for your units, here each faction is genuinely unique. Switching from Atreidies to Harkonnen to Smugglers to Fremen to Corrino feels almost like playing a different game each time. For example Fremen have very limited access to Landsraad voting which is a major element of major houses gameplay.You get a learn-as-you-go tutorial that explains the basics - indeed crucial to grasp the multitude of mechanics the game offers. I consider myself a veteran of RTS games and still wothout the tutorial I would have been hard pressed to figure out many things on my own.Map is semi-randomly generated area around the Arrakis' pole and issplit into sectors in a boardgame style. Each sector has a village, own resources and a set of bonuses. There are landmarks known from the books like Mount Idaho or the Barrier Wall, offering unique bonuses. You will feel the urge to take as many as you can, but it gets ever more expensive and ever more difficult to keep control of more territories as you face raids, enemy spies and attacks.

candidates.title: Age of Mythology: Retold review
candidates.text: I've been playing this game since the original came out over 20 years ago. I loved the original, it captured something special no other RTS game has managed to capture. Often times they are grounded in a type of realism that isn't bad, just always present. Age of Empires, Empire Earth, even Starcraft. All have their units and counters units, maybe some larger, interesting units, but nothing over the top. Age of Mythology said that cool factor trumps everything else. And it WORKED. Age of Mythology Retold is one of the most faithful remasters of a beloved game that's been released in some time. But they dared to go beyond that. They wanted to improve it, something that could be dangerous if they didn't understand what made the game so great. But they did understand and the improvements made this game even more than it was 20 years ago. Everything from quality of life, to balance, to straight up new content. And they did it so well. I knew this game like the back of my hand, yet here I am feeling like I'm playing it again for the first time, yet it's still the Age of Mythology I know and love. How do you even achieve that? Yet they managed it.If you love mythology, RTS games, MOBAs, or specifically loved Age of Mythology, you will love this game. The graphics are great, the mechanics are great, the spectacle of mythological monsters is so fun, and to top it off, it has one of the best stories of any RTS game out there. Definitely check it out if you're on the fence.

candidates.title: Age of Mythology: Retold review
candidates.text: The perfect example of how a remaster SHOULD be done. For those who don't know, it's Age of Empires with Gods and mythological creatures, as in it was literally made by the same studio. It's the same amazing game we remember with a beautiful visual update to give it a modern shine. They even give you the option to toggle the classic God/Goddess portraits if you want. But it didn't stop with just polishing what we had, this game actually brings several new features as well. For one, units have been re-balanced and some given new abilities (ex: Hydras couldnt regenerate in the original). God powers are no longer limited to a fixed amount of uses, the first one is free and then you can keep using them by spending favor. And lastly theyre adding completely new content. The Norse have a new god, and a brand new game mode has also been added.It doesn't even stop there though. If you've looked over the steam page, you may notice a certain something is actually missing. The core game and The Titans expansion are all here, but the embarassment that was "Tale of the Dragon" is no where to be seen. That's because it's been cast off, and we're actually getting an entirely new expansion themed around the Chinese Pantheon instead, and after that another expansion with an entirely new pantheon we haven't seen yet. The amount they're giving us with this is baffling. This isn't just a shinier version of the original, it's a BETTER one. Gives new life to an absolute classic

candidates.title: Age of Mythology: Retold review
candidates.text: A fantastic remake to an already amazing game, Retold elevates the play experience of Age of Mythology to another level. I have put hundreds of hours into the original AOM, the titans expansion, and extended edition, and none of them come close to the polish, readability, and fun of this game. The choice to have god powers be recastable lets the fun keeping into the hyper late game, and the fifth age added by wonders caps it off beautifully. It feels like every minor god got a new toy to play with, as well as significant balance changes and new toys for each faction, especially the Norse and Atlanteans. Speaking of the Norse, they were the first faction to get a new major god, with more following suite later. A traditionally aggressive faction, Freyr is the perfect defensive leader to add a more holistic identity to the faction. I already have about 55 hours in the game (Some of the time spent on my time played was idling), and just now finished all the single player content on Titan difficulty. In this time I have also dabbled a bit in the editor, and played an odd one or two skirmishes, and I know I will come back to play more. Even if you are not interested in multiplayer, the replayability this game offers can't be passed up. The setting, the music, the art style, and the charm of this game is a treat to anyone who gives it a fair shake. I am looking forward to the DLC coming out and can't recommend trying this game out enough!
